maya: quick note — I'm seeing duplicated request IDs across concurrent coroutines when using py-sdk async client + our OTEL middleware.

maya: minimal repro (super simplified):
```py
# minimal repro
from redwood import AsyncClient
import logging, asyncio

client = AsyncClient(api_key="x")
async def task(i):
    await client.generate("hi")
    logging.info("req_id %s", client._last_request_id)  # simplified

await asyncio.gather(*(task(i) for i in range(5)))
```

maya: output shows same req_id in multiple lines. Not sure if sdk is reusing contextvar or if middleware isn't copying traceparent.

sam: can you paste the exact log lines? and which SDK version?

maya: logs:
```
INFO:root:req_id abc123
INFO:root:req_id abc123
INFO:root:req_id abc123
```

maya: using python-sdk 0.14.2 (async client), otel-instrumentation 1.20, running uvloop.

jonas: likely contextvar leakage — our request-id sits in a contextvar set during send; but when using background tasks/taskgroup the context isn't always copied. There's an asyncio issue w/ context propagation across tasks sometimes.

linda: did you try wrapping tasks with contextvars.copy_context()? e.g.,

linda: ```py
import contextvars, asyncio
ctx = contextvars.copy_context()
asyncio.create_task(ctx.run(task, i))
```

sam: we already attempt to set request id inside the request coroutine before network call. Could be that our middleware sets request id on transport object (shared) rather than per-request. @maya can you repro with this simpler snippet that reads header sent?

maya: yes repro attached — gist: https://gist.github.com/maya/abc456
Repro shows header "x-request-id: abc123" included in concurrent requests.

jonas: ok that's a bug. I think transport session is reusing a header dict. Quick fix: clone header dict per request in async client send path. I can make PR.

sam: also let's add an integration test that spawns 50 concurrent tasks asserting unique request ids. Add to tests/async/test_request_id_propagation.py

maya: can you add also a note to docs explaining async caveat? onboarding pages often show naive asyncio.gather example.

linda: +1. Also consider adding OpenTelemetry span/span-id binding earlier in middleware so we can derive request id deterministically from span context when present.

tracing-bot: new issue created: #5234 — py-sdk: async request-id leak across concurrent tasks. Link: https://git.redwood.ai/issue/5234

sam: thanks — assigning to @jonas, mark as high priority for 0.15.0. Maya can you paste env (uvloop, python 3.11) and attach coredump if any.

maya: done. thx everyone. :pray:
